verdictScope: The V1 defect I constructed in t38 is closed, and the closure is falsifiable rather than asserted. On the committed revision the original failing call shape (a request with NO content) now yields a readable, decidable record; the decision path distinguishes a malformed-but-present record from a truly absent id with two different errors; a normalized request expires on captain silence with the requester preserved; the implementer's five new assertions provably go RED when the repair is reverted (8 pass / 5 fail) and GREEN on the shipped code (13 pass / 0 fail), so none of them is a tautology; the t36 end-to-end case still passes 10/10 with skills/** untouched; and the registry plus every named gate is green with counts matching the declaration.

criterion2_decisionDistinguishes.method: One call with an id that exists nowhere, one call with an id present in the queue file but written WITHOUT content (so the mailbox shape check rejects it and the normal reader sees nothing).

observedFixed.malformedError: interjection "broken" exists but is MALFORMED (present in the queue but not readable: the mailbox shape requires a non-empty string content and the identity fields); re-enqueue it with content, or inspect the queue file

criterion2_decisionDistinguishes.reading: The two cases are now distinguishable and the malformed case no longer masquerades as absence. The malformed record is still invisible to the normal reader by design, which is exactly why the raw-parse path is needed.

criterion3_expiry.reading: Captain silence now resolves into an explicit expiry and the requester identity survives, so the member can be told. Before the repair the same call expired nothing.

residualRisks: The repair is FORWARD-looking: it normalizes new enqueues and reports pre-existing malformed queue records loudly on the decision path. Whether any historical team state already contains a malformed interjection line was explicitly out of this task's scope, and my verification does not scan cross-session state — so the loud-error path is the containment for old rows, not a cleanup.

The end-to-end delivery of an approved request at a member step boundary remains unverified (a limitation declared by both the implementation and my t38 pass). What this task verifies is the request-side safety property, the decision record, and the now-working expiry; the round trip still needs a long-lived captain session with spawned members.

The A/B falsifiability proof depends on a pre-repair copy of the module. The recipe and the observed taps are preserved, but the copied tree itself was deleted to avoid embedding stale product code in evidence — a future re-run must rebuild it from the named commit.
